crie.title: Persist Original to Object Storage
crie.purpose: Store the original uploaded file exactly once in object storage and record the reference on repository.documents. After this workflow, callers carry only { documentId, sha256, storageKey, correlationId } and never the binary.
crie.roadmap: Object Storage PR-2. New artifact: nothing frozen is touched and WF-001 does NOT call this yet — the ingestion cutover is PR-4.
crie.identifier: Numbered SW-029, the lowest free id. SW-017 (used illustratively in the roadmap) is already WF-002's Metadata Filter, and SW-016 is already used twice in this repository (Orphan Sweep and WF-002's Requirement Analyzer). A third collision was not created.

contract.input: { documentId (UUID, REQUIRED — the row must already exist), correlationId } plus the original file as BINARY on property 'data'.
contract.output: { documentId, sha256, storageKey, storageBucket, contentType, byteSize, storedAt, correlationId, skippedUpload }
contract.precondition: repository.documents row for documentId EXISTS. This workflow writes the five storage columns (0030); it does not register documents. Decision D4: the caller generates documentId before the key is computed, because the key embeds it.

crie.decisions: D1 columns from migration 0030. D3 document_blobs deferred, so no integrity row is written here. D4 documentId is caller-generated and arrives as input. D5 erasure is out of scope — this workflow never deletes.

findings_applied.H2: The key's date partition is derived from repository.documents.uploaded_at, NEVER from wall-clock at upload time. Wall-clock would give a re-ingested document a second key under a new date and orphan the first object.
findings_applied.H3: An existing storage_key is trusted ONLY after the object is verified present. A non-null key whose object is missing falls through to upload rather than silently skipping.
findings_applied.H6: Byte size is gated against CRIE_STORAGE_MAX_BYTES before upload, so an oversized file fails here rather than after the expensive OCR step. Unset means no gate.
findings_applied.M2: Verify-on-write: after upload the stored object's reported size is compared to the uploaded byte count. Full re-hash verification belongs to the storage-integrity job (PR-6), not here.
findings_applied.probeE: content_type and the key's {ext} are derived from MAGIC BYTES of the downloaded file, never from the Google Drive mimeType. WF-001 downloads with googleFileConversion, so Google-native documents arrive as application/pdf while Drive still reports vnd.google-apps.*.
findings_applied.probeG: No signed URL is minted here, so none can reach the execution log. When SW-005 mints one (PR-3) it must be minted and consumed inside a single node — a URL emitted in any node's output is persisted in the executions table.

crie.runtime_config: Bucket and endpoint are read from the n8n ENVIRONMENT ($env.CRIE_STORAGE_ENDPOINT, $env.CRIE_STORAGE_BUCKET, $env.CRIE_STORAGE_MAX_BYTES). configuration/storage.yaml remains the authored source of truth (R-08, decision D2); deployment resolves {env} from it and sets these variables, exactly as it already does for $env.CRIE_ADMIN_SCHEDULE_CRON. No secret is read from $env: the storage key is an n8n CREDENTIAL, bound on import.
crie.credentials_on_import: BIND BEFORE USE. The two HTTP nodes declare generic header auth with NO credential attached, matching the Azure Document Intelligence pattern — attach the Supabase storage credential after import. The Postgres nodes use the existing CRIE Postgres credential (service_role/owner).
crie.testing_status: PENDING INFRASTRUCTURE. The upload and verify paths cannot be executed until a private bucket and a storage credential exist. Everything not requiring them is implemented and statically validated.

nodes.name: When Called by WF-001
nodes.notes: inputSource:'passthrough' (LOWERCASE t) per the frozen SW I/O contract — the camelCase variant is silently ignored on import and drops the caller's payload including binary. Receives { documentId, correlationId } plus the original file as binary property 'data'.

nodes.name: Load Document Row

parameters.query: SELECT id::text AS document_id, sha256, to_char(uploaded_at AT TIME ZONE 'UTC', 'YYYY/MM/DD') AS uploaded_partition, storage_key, storage_bucket FROM repository.documents WHERE id = '{{ $json.documentId }}';

nodes.notes: Reads the authoritative sha256 and the uploaded_at date partition (H2) for the caller's documentId. NOTE ON {{ }}: this is an INTENDED n8n interpolation of a UUID that resolves before the SQL runs (same pattern as SW-016's integer config) — it is NOT a forbidden literal {{token}} placeholder; no literal braces reach Postgres. alwaysOutputData:true so a MISSING row still reaches Prepare Object, which raises a clear error instead of the workflow ending silently on zero items.

nodes.name: Re-attach Binary
nodes.notes: Binary is re-established exactly once, at the point of use, per the Workflow Engineering Guidelines. Do not iterate this; iterative re-attachment is a symptom, not a fix.

nodes.name: Prepare Object
nodes.notes: Derives contentType/ext from magic bytes, gates size, and builds the key from uploaded_at + documentId + sha256. Raises rather than storing anything it cannot name correctly — an object keyed with the wrong extension is worse than a failed ingestion. Carries the binary forward for the upload node.

nodes.name: Existing key?
nodes.notes: H3: a non-null storage_key is NOT trusted on its own. True -> verify the object really exists; false -> upload.

nodes.name: Verify Existing Object
nodes.notes: H3: does the object behind the recorded key actually exist? onError + neverError so a 404 becomes data rather than a failure — a missing object must fall through to upload, not abort. BIND the Supabase storage credential on import.

nodes.name: Existing object present?
nodes.notes: True -> the stored original is intact; skip the upload (the duplicate path). False -> the key is stale and the object is gone; upload it.

nodes.name: Upload Original
nodes.notes: Stores the original exactly once. x-upsert:true makes re-uploading identical bytes to the same key a no-op instead of a 409 — required for retries to be safe (PR-0 probe C will confirm the exact semantics). Body is the binary itself; the bytes are never base64-expanded into JSON. BIND the Supabase storage credential on import.

nodes.name: Verify Stored Object
nodes.notes: M2 verify-on-write. Reads back the stored object's metadata; the next node asserts the size matches what was uploaded. Full re-hash verification is the storage-integrity job (PR-6), deliberately not done here. Unlike the existing-object check this node does NOT swallow errors: a failure to read back what we just wrote must fail the workflow.

nodes.name: Assert Stored Size
nodes.notes: Fails closed. If the read-back does not match, no storage_key is written — a document with a NULL key is recoverable; a document pointing at a corrupt object is not.

nodes.name: Write Storage Columns

parameters.query: UPDATE repository.documents SET storage_key = '{{ $json.storageKey }}', storage_bucket = '{{ $json.storageBucket }}', byte_size = {{ $json.byteSize }}, content_type = '{{ $json.contentType }}', stored_at = now() WHERE id = '{{ $json.documentId }}' RETURNING id::text AS document_id, storage_key, storage_bucket, byte_size, content_type, stored_at;

nodes.notes: Writes the five columns added by migration 0030. UPDATE only — this workflow never registers a document (decision D4: the caller owns documentId) and never deletes (decision D5). RETURNING makes the persisted values observable to the caller. NOTE ON {{ }}: intended n8n interpolation, resolved before the SQL runs.

nodes.name: Return to Caller
nodes.notes: Emits the reference tuple { documentId, sha256, storageKey, correlationId } plus the stored-object facts. From here the caller carries only this — never the binary.
